playbook:
PLAYBOOK

- Escort claims are free money and I left them on the table again. From round 1, file [salvage: someboat] every single round — never [salvage: none]. Naming costs nothing even if unreciprocated; a reciprocated pair pays 5 per round.
- The bigger failure this game: I proposed Foxtrot as a fixed escort partner in my note every round, and Foxtrot never once filed salvage back. No pair ever formed, all 6 rounds. Lesson: a silent partner is not a partner. Watch the salvage filings (they show up in the results) — if my named partner doesn't reciprocate for two straight rounds, publicly switch my proposal to the other live boat in my next note, and start filing my salvage on the new candidate. Keep rotating until someone bites. Don't anchor on one non-responder for six rounds.
- In the note, address a specific boat by name with a clear, simple ask: "Foxtrot, file salvage on Echo this round and I'll file on you." A vague broadcast got no takers; try explicit pairwise offers, and if round 2 passes with no response, try offering to the other boat too. A small side-payment framing ("I'll fire elsewhere / report your hits honestly") may help if plain asks fail.
- Never lie at the claim stage. The office validates claims against the true private result; a false claim gains nothing and burns credibility. When told hit, claim hit; when told miss, claim miss. This worked cleanly all game.
- Do not fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison is tempting, but the standing signal says firing there puts me off the board for the rest of the patrol — the whole remaining game. Never worth it.
- Follow the standing fire order (fire at the named next station). Defecting gains nothing since the target order is fixed and known to all.
- Vary my firing cell. My round-1 hit on cell 5 was followed by five straight misses at mostly the same cells. After a hit, fire an adjacent cell next round; after a miss, jump to a different region entirely. Also watch the target's observed pattern: if I've missed many times in one region, their hiding spots may be clustered elsewhere — cover the region I've never fired into.
- Vary my own hiding cell the same way: never camp one cell, move after being hit, avoid my own previous spots and obvious symmetry. Gamma hit me twice late while I dodged; pure unpredictability beats patterned dodging.
- Keep notes short and functional: use them for escort coordination and observable facts (who hit whom). Skip "steady on station" filler — it wastes the only dealmaking channel. But don't just repeat a proposal that has already been ignored; change the ask or the addressee.
- Track the scoreboard each round as a signal: who is accumulating (this game Foxtrot ran away with it via hits on Gamma) tells me who is being left alone and who is a viable escort partner. Escort income is the reliable income; prioritize locking a reciprocating pair over shooting optimization.
- Truthful claiming plus standing-order firing gave me a small positive score (+4, one hit) with zero downside. The shooting game alone is a low-variance small win; the escort pair is the only route to a big score, so treat finding a reciprocating partner as the main objective, not an afterthought.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Hiding.** When I have no information, hide mid-line (4-6). Once a hunter has targeted me repeatedly, break pattern: avoid my previous cells and pick off-beat numbers (2, 8, 9) rather than centre cells, since centre cells are the default guess. Track every shot fired at me and never reuse a cell I was hit in. Note: in this episode Echo fired at me every round and never hit — staying off the default centre cell (hiding at 8) worked. Keep doing that.

**Notes.** Station notes are public and free coordination. Use them to propose mutual escort deals explicitly: "Foxtrot will escort Echo; Echo, name Foxtrot." A mutual escort pays 5 points to each boat, more than a hit (4). But accept that bots may ignore proposals — Echo and Gamma posted only "steady on station" all game and never took any deal. Keep proposing anyway (it costs nothing), but don't build my plans around acceptance.

**Escorting.** Never default to [salvage: none]. Even without an agreement, guessing costs nothing and a mutual name pays 5. Pick the boat most likely to name me back — the boat that isn't shooting at me this round. My standing-order partner doesn't work: Echo (my predecessor in the picket) shot at me every round, but I named Echo every round anyway and never once got paid a mutual escort. So in this game I earned +15 entirely from shooting hits (three hits on Gamma) while my repeated [salvage: Echo] returned nothing. Conclusion: the default guess is harmless but worthless against non-responsive bots; the real income was hitting. Next time, spread my escort guesses — if my standing guess hasn't paid by round 3, try the third boat instead of repeating a dead guess. Escorted-escort payout is only worth pursuing if any boat ever responds in kind.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (fire at next station round the picket). My shots at Gamma: fired 5 twice (one hit round 1, miss round 6), and the record shows hits in rounds 4 and 5 as well. Firing at the target's previously-used cells paid off repeatedly — Gamma apparently reused or stayed near cells I'd hit. Track my target's past hide cells (learned from my own hits and misses) and fire at cells they've actually used; only default to centre (5) when I have no data. Keep a private log every round of where I fired and the result, and use it.

**Harbor.** Firing on Harbor pays 3 points regardless, but Harbor threatens removal for the rest of the patrol. Only worth it on the final round if I'm behind, or if I'm far enough ahead that losing future rounds doesn't matter. In this game I was ahead on points, so leaving Harbor alone was right.

**Claims.** Always report the true result. Claims are validated against the private result, so lying is impossible anyway. No change.

**Scoring math — revised.** Hit = +4 shooter, -1 target. Mutual escort = +5 each but requires the other boat to actually name me — against non-responsive bots this is pure fantasy income. In this episode shooting was 100% of my score. So: prioritize shooting accuracy (track target hide-cell history) over escort schemes, but keep spending notes and guesses on escort attempts since they cost nothing. Escort deals are the upside if I ever meet a responsive player; shooting is the reliable floor.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

Claims: the office forces the claim to match the true shot result, so I just repeat the true result every time. Never reason that a false claim "hides" anything; it doesn't and only risks a penalty.

Escort stage: still the biggest income source in theory (mutual claim = +5 per round, worth more than a hit), but this episode proved the hard part is reciprocation. I named Echo every round and used my notes to propose pairings explicitly ("Gamma escorts Echo — name me back") and Echo still never claimed me. Result: zero escort income all game, and I finished at -4. Lessons: (1) Always name a live boat rather than none — that part stands. (2) Watch the other boats' actual escort behavior and claims in the early rounds; if a boat never reciprocates after two rounds, switch my claim to the boat that does reciprocate (Foxtrot was scoring heavily this game — 15 points — which suggests it was collecting escort income somewhere; I should have looked at who was naming whom and joined that pair). (3) Notes proposing a pairing are worth one try, not six — if the proposal is ignored, stop repeating it and pick a different partner or mirror whatever pairing the other two boats have formed. (4) If I am ever the only boat being systematically excluded, naming either of the other two still costs nothing and keeps the option open.

Firing: follow the standing order — firing at Harbor is not worth the 3 points against removal from the board. But fix the guessing: I fired cell 5 at Echo in every single round and never hit. Re-firing the same cold cell round after round is the marksmanship failure, not just re-firing a known-cold cell after they "move." Track my own shot history against each target and cover new cells each round (spread across 4, 5, 6, then outward); a target that dodges mid cells is likely on an edge. When a target's cell becomes unknown again after a hit, definitely spread — but also spread when the same cell has missed repeatedly.

Hiding: switch cells after absorbing a hit — that stands. But I got hit twice this game while shuffling around the middle; being hit twice cost me only -2 total (hits cost the target just 1 point), so don't over-invest in dodging. After being hit, move to a genuinely different region (e.g., from mid to an edge like 2 or 8), not just an adjacent mid cell. Otherwise any cell is roughly equal.

Scoring math to guide priorities: mutual escort = +5/round, hit = +4, being hit = -1. Being hit is cheap; landing hits and escort income are where the money is. The plan each round still holds — fire at the ordered target at a *fresh* cell, claim truthfully, always file an escort claim naming a live boat — but with the escort claim now aimed at whoever actually reciprocates, observed from play, not at whoever I proposed to in a note.

Endgame check (rounds 5-6): with few rounds left and no escort pair established, don't keep begging the same boat in notes; either swap partners or accept the firing game and focus shot coverage. Repeating a failed note is a wasted slot.
